title: CI: fail fast on hangs and attestation drift
body:
The 2026-08-13 outage was a one-line comment change that unregistered every provider. The bug was trivial. What made it cost **ten days** was that nothing failed fast.

Three guards, all verified against a reproduction of that exact regression.

## 1. Bounded gate waits

`tests/test_broker.py` had two tests that `await` an `asyncio.Event` a skipped provider never sets. With no timeout they hang forever — which is how one stale hash consumed the 6h job ceiling on three Python versions on every push.

Both waits now go through `_await_gate()`, which fails after 10s naming the likely cause:

```
AssertionError: timed out after 10s waiting for the provider to enter search;
the provider was almost certainly skipped before execution
(check ProviderReadinessSnapshot.execution_decision)
```

## 2. Job wall-clock ceilings

**No job in `ci.yml` declared `timeout-minutes`**, so every job inherited GitHub's 6h default. Each now declares one sized to its work — test 20, postgres-ledger 20, image-build 30, scorecard 15, production-config 10, freshness 10. This bounds *any* future hang, not just this one.

## 3. Attestation drift checked before the suite

`scripts/generate_provider_fixture_attestations.py --check` already existed, but ran only in `postgres-ledger` — which does not gate the test job. So drift surfaced as a six-hour hang instead of a one-line message. The test job now runs it *before* pytest.

## Verified by re-breaking it

Drifting `shared_adapter_sha256` across all 14 providers reproduces the original failure:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| attestation drift detected | never (only in a non-gating job) | **0s** |
| the two hanging tests | hang forever → 6h ceiling | **fail in 20s** |

Then restored and confirmed clean.

Full suite: **2666 passed, 43 skipped**. `ruff check`: clean. `ci.yml` validates as YAML.

title: Reject a modern MCP request that omits MCP-Protocol-Version, and pin the transport contract
body:
I measured the pinned SDK against the [2026-07-28 Streamable HTTP spec](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/transports/streamable-http) instead of assuming. **This corrects my earlier report** — most of what I flagged as gaps is already handled.

## What was already correct (SDK, not Argus)

| requirement | observed |
|---|---|
| GET / DELETE rejected | `405` |
| no session minted or echoed; client-supplied `Mcp-Session-Id` ignored | verified |
| `server/discover` implemented | `200` |
| header/body protocol mismatch | `400` + `-32020` |
| missing or mismatched `Mcp-Method` | `400` + `-32020` |
| missing or mismatched `Mcp-Name` | `400` + `-32020` |
| unsupported version lists supported revisions | `400` + `-32022` with `data.supported` |
| unknown method | `404` + `-32601` |

Twelve of thirteen. No Argus change needed for any of them.

## The one real gap

The spec permits treating a request with **no** `MCP-Protocol-Version` header as `2025-03-26` for pre-2025-06-18 clients, and the SDK does exactly that. But a body carrying `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` is unambiguously a modern request — so serving it under legacy semantics **silently downgrades it**, which is the one outcome ADR 0006's compatibility contract forbids:

> Its protocol branch is selected per request and cannot silently downgrade a valid modern request.

That combination now returns `400` with `-32020` `HeaderMismatch`. Genuine header-less legacy `initialize` traffic is unaffected — asserted directly, not assumed.

## Why the test file is mostly testing the SDK

`tests/test_mcp_2026_07_28_contract.py` pins all fourteen behaviors, and that's deliberate. Argus depends on this behavior but doesn't own it, and **there was previously no test covering any of it** — the SDK could regress and change what real clients receive with nothing failing. Now it fails here.

## Known constraint, recorded not fixed

`stateless_http=True` affects only the legacy leg: it drops sticky-routing requirements but **disables the legacy back channel**, raising `NoBackChannelError` for a tool that needs one. No Argus tool takes a `Context` parameter today, so nothing depends on it. Recorded in ADR 0006 as a trade-off to re-open when a tool wants progress notifications — not a latent bug. (This also corrects my earlier framing of it as an active risk.)

ADR 0006 gains a dated amendment with the measured matrix, which row Argus owns, and that constraint.

## Verification

Full suite: **2662 passed, 43 skipped**. `ruff check`: clean.

title: Security: stop persisting a raw bearer token in `argus mcp init`
body:
`argus mcp init --url ...` leaked the bearer token **four** ways. Only the first was previously flagged.

| # | leak | where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `export ARGUS_API_KEY=<token>` appended to `~/.zshrc` / `~/.bashrc` | plaintext on disk, in every future shell |
| 2 | literal token as an `Authorization` header | `.mcp.json` |
| 3 | literal token as an `Authorization` header | OpenCode config |
| 4 | token printed inside a copy-paste `gemini mcp add -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"` | terminal → shell history when run |

`.mcp.json` is gitignored, so #2 was not a commit risk — but all four put a long-lived credential somewhere it outlives the command.

## Fix

The command now records only a **reference** and never reads, stores, or prints the value.

- `.mcp.json` and OpenCode → `Authorization: Bearer ${ARGUS_API_KEY}`. Claude Code [documents `${VAR}` expansion](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp) for precisely this case (`"Authorization": "Bearer ${API_KEY}"`).
- Codex → keeps `bearer_token_env_var`, now honouring the configured name.
- Gemini → prints `$ARGUS_API_KEY` for the shell to expand at run time, so history holds the reference.
- Shell-profile write → **deleted**. The command tells the operator to export the variable themselves.

`--key` is removed and exits with an explanatory error rather than silently behaving differently. `--token-env-var NAME` replaces it (default `ARGUS_API_KEY`) and rejects an argument that doesn't look like an env-var name — so a token pasted into the wrong flag fails loudly instead of landing on disk.

This also matches what the repo already documented but did not do: *"Codex stores only the environment variable name in `~/.codex/config.toml`."*

## Verification

Tests assert the negative directly: after invoking `mcp init` with a real token in the environment, the literal value must appear in **no** generated file under `HOME` and in **no** printed output, and an existing `~/.zshrc` must be byte-unchanged.

Confirmed end-to-end with a live secret exported:

```
$ HOME=... ARGUS_API_KEY="sk-LIVE-SECRET-9999" argus mcp init --global --client all --url https://...
  gemini mcp add argus https://.../mcp -t http -H "Authorization: Bearer $ARGUS_API_KEY"
  Export ARGUS_API_KEY in the shell that launches Codex; argus never stores the token itself.

$ grep -rl "sk-LIVE-SECRET-9999" $HOME
(no matches)
```

Full suite: **2652 passed, 43 skipped**. `ruff check`: clean.

## Breaking change

`--key` is gone. It is a security-motivated removal, so it errors with a message pointing at `--token-env-var` rather than being quietly accepted. CHANGELOG, README, and `docs/troubleshooting.md` updated — the troubleshooting page previously *instructed* users to put the secret in their rc file.

title: Design: request-class-aware research admission, enforced at the workflow boundary
body:
Brings in the Homelab authority design and plan, with two review decisions applied. Docs only — no source, deployment, secret, or provider change.

## Decision 1 — the flat 3/2 floor is withdrawn

The original design admitted research at "3 usable citations across 2 registrable domains" for everything. Two measured reasons to drop it.

**It sits below observed output, so it would never fire.** The 2026-08-09 production benchmark in `docs/research/2026-08-09-argus-tonight-acceptance.md` recorded:

| | system | independent audit |
|---|---|---|
| usable sources | **11** | 9 |
| registrable domains | **7** | 7 |
| primary sources | **4** | 3 |

A 3/2 floor is roughly half of already-achieved output.

**More importantly, counting sources does not catch the failure that actually happened.** That same run *passed* the numeric floor and still **failed** its evidence gate:

> Source floor — VERIFIED numerically, 11 sources / 7 domains / 4 primary
> Citation integrity — **FAILED**, the report claims a `/web-research` URL absent from the manifest citation set

An unsupported claim standing beside eleven genuine citations satisfies any counting rule. So per-claim resolution is the check with teeth; counts are a secondary guard.

**A flat floor is also wrong for single-source lookups.** A canonical factual question answered from one authoritative primary source must not be refused.

Requirements now key on the `EXECUTABLE_REQUEST_CLASSES` that already exist in `argus/broker/readiness.py:27`:

| class | requirement |
|---|---|
| `discovery`, `grounding` | one usable citation that supports the answer |
| `research` | 5 usable citations / 3 registrable domains / 2 primary |
| `recovery` | as the recovery target requires, minimum one |
| **every class** | **every material claim resolves to an emitted citation** |

Adopting 5/3/2 for `research` matches the release gate already declared in `argus/acceptance_v3/bundle.py` (`_COMPLETED_MIN_URLS = 5`, `_COMPLETED_MIN_DOMAINS = 3`, `_COMPLETED_MIN_PRIMARY = 2`), so the codebase carries one evidence standard instead of two that disagree.

The plan now requires **extracting** the existing `minimum_evidence()` and `tld`-backed `_registrable_domain` into a shared module rather than writing a third implementation — `argus/workflows/targeted_research.py:211` already holds a second copy.

These numbers are provisional until Task 12 measures ordinary traffic rather than one curated benchmark. Changing them is a recorded decision, not a silent constant edit.

## Decision 2 — admission moves to the workflow boundary

`build_research_pack` is the existing targeted-research MCP tool. The original plan gated only the new `POST /api/research` route, which would have left the old tool as an unchecked path into the same workflow — making admission decorative.

The check now lives inside `argus/workflows/targeted_research.py` / `service.py`, so `build_research_pack`, `POST /api/research`, and `research_web` all inherit it structurally rather than each route remembering to ask. Added a guard test that enumerates registered research surfaces and fails if any reaches targeted research without traversing admission, so a future surface cannot silently reopen the gap.

`search_web` is explicitly out of scope — different operation, unchanged semantics.

## Not decided here

The MCP contract gaps found while verifying the spec against the 2026-07-28 sources remain open: exact error codes (`-32020` HeaderMismatch, `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion), `404`/`-32601` for unknown method, mandatory header-body match validation, GET/DELETE → `405`, and that `stateless_http=True` disables the legacy back channel (`NoBackChannelError`). Also unaddressed: Argus currently mints an `mcp-session-id` for an `initialize` carrying `protocolVersion: 2026-07-28`, which the spec forbids.

title: Unblock CI: regenerate stale provider fixture attestations and port MCP tests to SDK v2
body:
## Why CI has been red for 10 days

Commit `7e7c1f8` (labeled `docs: record stateless MCP compatibility boundary`) changed **one comment line** in `argus/config.py`:

```diff
- # Parse ARGUS_CALLER_TIER_CAPS=clio*:1,hermes*:1
+ # Parse ARGUS_CALLER_TIER_CAPS=hermes*:1,mac-agents:1,maya:1
```

`config.py` is one of the 12 files hashed into `shared_adapter_sha256`, so that comment drifted the hash and invalidated **all 14** provider fixture attestations:

`verify_fixture_attestation` → False → `compatible_fixture_release=False` → `incompatible_fixture_release` → `registered=False` → **every provider skipped at execution**.

That surfaced as four `tests/test_broker.py` failures asserting `'skipped' == 'success'`, and as an **unbounded hang** in two more — both `await` an `asyncio.Event` that a skipped provider never sets. CI hit the 6h job ceiling on Python 3.11, 3.12 and 3.13 on every push since 2026-08-13. The `postgres-ledger` "Verify canonical provider fixture attestations" failure shares this root cause.

## What this PR does

**`6769e08` — regenerate attestations.** Ran the existing `scripts/generate_provider_fixture_attestations.py`. Restores provider registration; the hang disappears.

**`d3ef73f` — port the MCP suites to the `mcp==2.0.0` baseline already in source.** Not all mechanical; three were real v2 API moves:

- `transport_security` / `json_response` moved off the `MCPServer` constructor onto `streamable_http_app()`/`sse_app()`. **Relocated, not dropped** — the `allowed_hosts` binding is load-bearing (the SDK otherwise rejects the TestClient `Host`), and the network-serve test asserts it as a security property.
- `call_tool()` returns a single `CallToolResult`, not a `(content, structured)` tuple.
- The **wire format did not change**: `structuredContent`/`isError` remain the JSON keys (pydantic aliases). Only Python attributes went snake_case. Verified with `model_dump(by_alias=True)` — a blanket string rename would have broken the protocol while keeping tests green.

Contract corrections to match what source already declares: `transport_version` → `2026-07-28`, and `SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS` now advertises `2026-07-28`. Added `LEGACY_HANDSHAKE_PROTOCOLS` for the parametrized handshake tests, since `2026-07-28` removed both `initialize` and protocol sessions.

Also pins `actions/checkout` in `ai-review.yml` to the full SHA already used by the other ten workflow steps (the repo's own supply-chain policy test was failing), and drops a pre-existing unused import flagged by ruff.

## Verification

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest -q` | 42 failed, **6h timeout ×3 versions** | **2648 passed, 43 skipped** (exit 0, 52s) |
| `ruff check argus tests` | 1 error | All checks passed |
| attestation `--check` | stale | passes |

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

1. **No timeout guard on the broker tests.** `await entered.wait()` with no `asyncio.wait_for` turns any provider-skip regression into a 6-hour burn instead of a 1-second failure. That is what made a comment change cost 10 days.
2. **Nothing fails fast on attestation drift.** `--check` exists but runs only in `postgres-ledger`, which does not gate the test job — so the symptom is a hang rather than a clear error.
3. Argus's session registry mints an `mcp-session-id` for an `initialize` carrying `protocolVersion: 2026-07-28`. Per spec a modern revision gets no session, and `initialize` implies a legacy client. Source behavior deliberately unchanged here — flagged for the MCP contract review.

title: Fix Maya outbox premature receipt timeouts
body:
## Summary

- Align the Maya outbox HTTP read timeout with the configured delivery timeout.
- Keep the existing total wall-clock deadline and bounded receipt response budget.
- Add local delayed-response, deadline, receipt-budget, and idempotency regression coverage.
- Document the operator-visible reliability fix in the Unreleased changelog.

## Root cause

`MayaOutboxDispatcher` configured `httpx.Timeout(..., read=min(1.0, timeout))`. Maya health/receipt responses can legitimately take longer than one second, so the client raised `ReadTimeout` before the configured delivery budget elapsed and moved each claimed row to retry.

The transport read budget now matches the configured delivery timeout; `_post_with_total_deadline` continues to check the wall-clock deadline and enforce the 64 KiB receipt budget.

## Validation

- `uv run --no-sync pytest -q` — 2308 passed, 43 skipped, 4 unrelated Starlette deprecation warnings.
- `uv run --no-sync pytest -q tests/test_maya_outbox.py` — 142 passed, 3 skipped.

title: Implement hermetic scorecard and immutable candidate evidence bundle
body:
## Question

Implement S10 hermetic scorecard and immutable candidate evidence bundle so the complete S0-S9 release candidate produces a deterministic stability verdict and a validated, checksummed, secret-free evidence bundle.

## Scope and acceptance

- Follow Task 15 in `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-27-retrieval-evidence-mechanical-port.md` exactly.
